svg.aria-label: A brass desk orrery of the Earth and Moon on a round plinth. A crank turns a two-stage gear train, 10 to 39 and 10 to 70, so 27.3 turns of the crank, one per day, carry the Moon once round the Earth. The Earth globe leans 23.4 degrees on its axle. A lit wire held by fine stays on the arms traces a ballistic lunar transfer: it leaves the Earth, swings out beyond the Moon's orbit and falls back to be captured in a loop round the Moon, with a small spacecraft bead on the return leg.
